issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the Dashboards author filter search, the bolded part of an author name is missing or on the wrong letters for Korean names and for accented names stored in decomposed form.

## User Impact

When you search the author list (shown once there are more than 8 authors), the matched part of each name is bolded correctly, for example `민` in `김민수`, `Lee` in `Kim 민수 Lee`, and `García` for the search `garcia`. Which authors match does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`AuthorName` found the match position in the folded name (NFD, accents removed, lowercased), then used that position and the raw query length to slice the original name. Folding changes string length: Hangul syllables split into 2–3 jamo, and decomposed accents are dropped. So the offsets did not line up.

`matchFoldedQuery` in `ui/src/lib/text-match.ts` finds the match in the folded name, then maps it back to the original name by folding each prefix of the name and comparing lengths. Combining marks right after the match stay with the last matched letter. The filter and the highlight share one `foldSearchText`, the same fold the filter used before, so which authors match does not change, and Greek final sigma (`ΝΙΚΟΣ` vs `νικος`) still matches.

## Evidence

Real Gateway with the built Control UI, in Chromium (Playwright), node 24.22.1 in Docker. Ten dashboards, each created by its own user profile, including `김민수`, `Kim 민수 Lee`, `García` stored decomposed and `ΝΙΚΟΣ`. Two runs on main and two on this PR: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196639#issuecomment-6770011657).

| Search | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `민` | `김민수`: nothing bold | `민` in both names |
| `lee` | nothing bold | `Lee` |
| `garcia` | `Garcí` bold, final `a` plain | `García` |

The list of matching authors is the same on main and this PR for every search. `ada`, `νικος`, `ΝΙΚΟΣ` and an empty search behave the same on both.

![Before: main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6627c153-b07e-4b65-9505-a64c8f6d416b)
![After: this PR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/205df377-1a0e-4c77-8bf5-5de8fe80aecf)

- `ui/src/lib/text-match.test.ts` covers the mapping for Hangul (partial syllable), mixed scripts, a decomposed accent at the end of the match, Greek final sigma and an empty search.
- Control UI gzip: chat boot JS +40 B, startup JS +0 B.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: UI display only, no stored data or contracts. If it is wrong, only the bold span in the Dashboards author search is affected.

issue.title: Label raw imager pixel spacing lengths as mm at detector
issue.body:
## Summary

Most of #1011 is already in `develop`: `getPixelSpacing` falls back to Imager Pixel Spacing, and #1996 added the magnification correction. The missing piece was the unit label. Lengths from raw Imager Pixel Spacing were shown as plain `mm`.

- `dicomImage.js`: new `getLengthUnit(elements)`. It returns `unit.mmDetector` only for Imager Pixel Spacing with no magnification factor. Every other spacing stays `unit.mm`; no spacing stays `unit.pixel`.
- `imageFactory.js`: `meta.lengthUnit` comes from `getLengthUnit`.
- `i18n.js`: new keys `unit.mmDetector` ("mm (detector)") and `unit.cm2Detector` ("cm² (detector)"). Apps can override them like the other units.
- New `src/math/units.js`: `getSurfaceValue` replaces the mm to cm² code copied in circle, ellipse and rectangle. Detector mm maps to detector cm².
- `maskImage.js`: uses `isMillimetreUnit`, so mask volumes stay in ml as before.
- `dicomCode.js`: the new units export to SR as UCUM `mm` / `cm2`, instead of the no-unit code `1`.

Standard refs (PS3.3 2024a):

- [C.8.11.4](https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/2024a/output/chtml/part03/sect_C.8.11.4.html): Imager Pixel Spacing is at the front plane of the detector housing and "shall never be adjusted" for magnification.
- [10.7.1.1](https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/2024a/output/chtml/part03/sect_10.7.html): Pixel Spacing is the distance in the patient.
- [C.8.11.5](https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/2024a/output/chtml/part03/sect_C.8.11.5.html): Estimated Radiographic Magnification Factor is SID/SOD, which supports the existing correction.

## Open questions

1. Should Pixel Spacing with Pixel Spacing Calibration Type (0028,0A02) get its own label? Left as `mm`.
2. Should magnification-corrected spacing be labelled as an estimate (e.g. "mm (est.)")? Left as `mm`.
3. Reading an SR back maps UCUM `mm` to `unit.mm`, so the detector label is lost on round trip.
4. Masks on raw detector images still report volume in ml, as before.

## Tests

- Written first and confirmed failing: `tests/dicom/dicomImage.test.js`, `dicomCode.test.js`, `tests/utils/i18n.test.js`, `tests/math/circle.test.js`, `tests/image/imageFactory.test.js`, new `tests/math/units.test.js`.
- `yarn lint` clean. `yarn build-ci` passes, `dwv.api.md` unchanged.
- Full vitest run: 1699/1700. The known local failure is `tests/app/toolboxController.test.js` ("enableShortcuts(false) stops keydown forwarding"), also on clean `develop`.
- Not checked by eye in the viewer.

Fixes #1011

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the IRC bot can send a fallback nick longer than 30 characters when its configured nick is 28–29 characters long and the nick is taken more than once in the same process.

## User Impact

User impact: an IRC bot with a long nick now recovers from repeated nick collisions with a nick that stays within the 30-character cap, instead of sending an over-long `NICK` that the server truncates (and may collide again) or rejects with 432, which fails the connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildFallbackNick` only truncated when the base nick alone was already at the cap. The suffix grows with the collision counter (`_`, `_2`, `_10`, …), so a 29-character base plus `_2` produced 31 characters. The check now compares base plus suffix against the cap, so truncation kicks in whenever the suffix would push the nick past 30.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway proof against a real IRC server

Setup, same for both runs:
- [Ergo](https://github.com/ergochat/ergo) IRC server in Docker on loopback, default config with `limits.nicklen: 30`.
- A separate client holds the nick `openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl` (29 characters) and WHOISes the fallback nicks every 5 s.
- Isolated Gateway (`OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` in a temp dir), plaintext loopback, two IRC accounts `first` and `second` both configured with that nick. Both connect at startup in one process, so the second collision gets the `_2` suffix.

**Before:** published `openclaw@2026.11.2` with `@openclaw/irc@2026.11.2` (`openclaw plugins install`), `openclaw gateway run`:

```text
[irc] [first] starting IRC provider (127.0.0.1:16667)
[irc] [second] starting IRC provider (127.0.0.1:16667)
[irc] [first] channel exited: IRC login failed (432): Erroneous nickname
[irc] [first] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[irc] [first] channel exited: IRC login failed (432): Erroneous nickname
[irc] [first] auto-restart attempt 2/10 in 10s
[irc] [first] channel exited: IRC login failed (432): Erroneous nickname
[irc] [first] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 21s
[irc] [first] channel exited: IRC login failed (432): Erroneous nickname
[irc] [first] auto-restart attempt 4/10 in 40s
```

Holder WHOIS: `openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl_` exists (`second`); `openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl_2` does not. Each auto-restart takes a new counter value (`_3`, `_4`, …), which is still 31 characters, so `first` never connects.

**After:** this branch from source (`pnpm build`, then `pnpm openclaw gateway run`):

```text
[irc] [first] starting IRC provider (127.0.0.1:16667)
[irc] [second] starting IRC provider (127.0.0.1:16667)
```

No 432 and no auto-restart in the Gateway log. Holder WHOIS from the server:

```text
:ergo.test 311 openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl openclawproofnickabcdefghijk_2 ~u cdvi2duzrc4jw.irc * OpenClaw
:ergo.test 311 openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl_ ~u cdvi2duzrc4jw.irc * OpenClaw
:ergo.test 401 openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl openclawproofnickabcdefghijkl_2 :No such nick
```

Both accounts are registered; the second uses the 30-character `openclawproofnickabcdefghijk_2`.

### Unit test


Added a 29-character case to the existing "normalizes and bounds fallback" test in `extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts`.

- Without the fix: `pnpm test extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` fails the new case with `expected 31 to be less than or equal to 30`.
- With the fix: 43/43 tests in the file pass.
- `pnpm format:check` and `oxlint` on both touched files: clean.

issue.body:
### Observed Behavior

When the function loop stops early, it makes one last call with `tool_choice="none"` (`core/_tools.py`, ~line 6011). This happens on `max_iterations`, `max_function_calls` or `max_duration_seconds`. For that call, `BedrockChatClient` drops `toolConfig` entirely (`_chat_client.py`, ~line 476), because Converse has no `"none"` tool choice.

At that point the conversation already contains `toolUse` and `toolResult` blocks. Converse requires `toolConfig` whenever those blocks are present. So the last request carries tool blocks with no tool config.

### Expected Behavior

When the conversation has `toolUse` or `toolResult` blocks, the last request still sends `toolConfig.tools`, without a `toolChoice`. `toolConfig` is only dropped when there are no tool blocks, as today.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the script below. It uses a fake Bedrock runtime that records each Converse request.

### Minimal Reproduction

```python
import asyncio

from agent_framework import Message
from agent_framework.amazon import BedrockChatClient


class FakeRuntime:
    """Returns a toolUse on the first Converse call and text afterwards, and records each request."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[dict] = []

    def converse(self, **request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        if len(self.requests) == 1:
            content, stop = [{"toolUse": {"toolUseId": "t1", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Paris"}}}], "tool_use"
        else:
            content, stop = [{"text": "Sunny."}], "end_turn"
        return {
            "output": {"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": content}},
            "stopReason": stop,
            "usage": {"inputTokens": 1, "outputTokens": 1, "totalTokens": 2},
        }


def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get the weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny in {city}"


async def main() -> None:
    runtime = FakeRuntime()
    client = BedrockChatClient(
        model="anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0",
        region="us-east-1",
        client=runtime,
        function_invocation_configuration={"max_iterations": 1},
    )
    await client.get_response([Message("user", ["Weather in Paris?"])], options={"tools": [get_weather]})

    final = runtime.requests[-1]
    blocks = [next(iter(block)) for message in final["messages"] for block in message["content"]]
    print("blocks in final request:", blocks)
    print("toolConfig in final request:", "toolConfig" in final)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Output on main:

```
blocks in final request: ['text', 'toolUse', 'toolResult']
toolConfig in final request: False
```

### Package Versions

`microsoft/agent-framework` main at `b8b350571` (editable install)

### Python Version

3.12.10

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Regression

Unknown

### Additional Context

Against real Bedrock, this request should fail with Converse's validation error: "The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks." I haven't run it against live Bedrock. If so, any Bedrock agent that hits an iteration or function-call limit errors instead of returning its final answer. #4529 and #4535 replaced the earlier `{"none": {}}` error with this one in the same scenario.

Possible fix: keep `toolConfig` for `"none"` when any message has a `toolUse` or `toolResult` block. Trade-off: the model still sees the tools on that last call. Without `toolChoice` it may still try to call one, but today the request fails outright.

I have this with a test in `test_bedrock_client.py`. It fails on main and passes with the fix. The bedrock package tests pass (106 passed, 1 skipped). I'd like to open the PR once the direction is confirmed.

Searched: "toolConfig field must be defined", "bedrock toolConfig", "bedrock tool_choice none", "bedrock max_iterations", "bedrock toolResult toolConfig". Related: #4529, #4535, #5165, #5172. None of them cover the tool-history case.

- [x] I personally verified this behavior and the reproduction details are authentic.
- [x] I will wait for explicit maintainer agreement before starting implementation of a non-trivial change.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a LINE table cell with an email link like `[bob@example.com](mailto:bob@example.com)` shows the address twice, as `bob@example.com (mailto:bob@example.com)`.

## User Impact

User impact: email links in LINE table cards now read `bob@example.com`, the same as the same link outside a table. Two-column tables that contain only such links keep the receipt-card layout instead of falling back to the generic styled table.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plain-text path already skips the `(href)` suffix when the label equals the href without `mailto:`. The table-cell path only compared the label to the raw href, so it appended the suffix and marked the cell as styled markup. Both paths now call one shared check, so they cannot drift apart again.

## Evidence

Built Gateway proof (main vs this branch, two runs each, CLI and Gateway delivery, with controls): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196636#issuecomment-6771189416

Test in `extensions/line/src/markdown-to-line.test.ts` (folded into the existing empty-cells table test): a table with the mailto link must render the same card as the same table with plain text.

- Without the fix: the test fails. A probe of `processLineMessage` shows the cell text `bob@example.com (mailto:bob@example.com)`.
- With the fix: the cell text is `bob@example.com`. `pnpm test extensions/line/src --maxWorkers=1` passes 59 files (523 tests, 1 skipped).
- `pnpm format:check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean.



### Real behavior proof

Delivery proof through the shipped `openclaw message send --channel line` path.

Setup:
- Before: published `openclaw@2026.11.2` with `@openclaw/line` from npm.
- After: this branch, built with `pnpm build`, run with `node openclaw.mjs`.
- Both runs used isolated state and a fake token. `HTTPS_PROXY` pointed at a local mitmproxy. A script there answered `api.line.me` locally with 200 and logged the request body. Nothing reached the real LINE API.

Command (same for both):

```
openclaw message send --channel line --target U0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --message "| Name | Contact |
|---|---|
| Bob | [bob@example.com](mailto:bob@example.com) |"
```

Both printed `✅ Sent via LINE. Message ID: 1`. Text nodes in the captured `POST /v2/bot/message/push` Flex body:

| Build | Flex text nodes |
|---|---|
| 2026.11.2 | `"Name"`, `"Contact"`, `"Bob"`, `"bob@example.com (mailto:bob@example.com)"` |
| this branch | `"Name / Contact"`, `"Bob"`, `"bob@example.com"` |

The branch sends the address once. It also picks the receipt-card layout, the same one a plain `bob@example.com` cell gets.

`formatByteSize` chose the unit before rounding. A value like 1,048,575 bytes stays in KiB (1023.999…) and then rounds to "1024". issue.body:
### Observed Behavior

When the function loop stops early, it makes one last call with `tool_choice="none"` (`core/_tools.py`, ~line 6011). This happens on `max_iterations`, `max_function_calls` or `max_duration_seconds`. For that call, `BedrockChatClient` drops `toolConfig` entirely (`_chat_client.py`, ~line 476), because Converse has no `"none"` tool choice.

At that point the conversation already contains `toolUse` and `toolResult` blocks. Converse requires `toolConfig` whenever those blocks are present. So the last request carries tool blocks with no tool config.

### Expected Behavior

When the conversation has `toolUse` or `toolResult` blocks, the last request still sends `toolConfig.tools`, without a `toolChoice`. `toolConfig` is only dropped when there are no tool blocks, as today.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the script below. It uses a fake Bedrock runtime that records each Converse request.

### Minimal Reproduction

```python
import asyncio

from agent_framework import Message
from agent_framework.amazon import BedrockChatClient


class FakeRuntime:
    """Returns a toolUse on the first Converse call and text afterwards, and records each request."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[dict] = []

    def converse(self, **request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        if len(self.requests) == 1:
            content, stop = [{"toolUse": {"toolUseId": "t1", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Paris"}}}], "tool_use"
        else:
            content, stop = [{"text": "Sunny."}], "end_turn"
        return {
            "output": {"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": content}},
            "stopReason": stop,
            "usage": {"inputTokens": 1, "outputTokens": 1, "totalTokens": 2},
        }


def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get the weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny in {city}"


async def main() -> None:
    runtime = FakeRuntime()
    client = BedrockChatClient(
        model="anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0",
        region="us-east-1",
        client=runtime,
        function_invocation_configuration={"max_iterations": 1},
    )
    await client.get_response([Message("user", ["Weather in Paris?"])], options={"tools": [get_weather]})

    final = runtime.requests[-1]
    blocks = [next(iter(block)) for message in final["messages"] for block in message["content"]]
    print("blocks in final request:", blocks)
    print("toolConfig in final request:", "toolConfig" in final)


asyncio.run(main())
```

issue.body:
## Observed Behavior

Foundry hosting's `_OutputItemTracker` adds usage updates even when they specify `merge_mode="replace"`.

Given cumulative snapshots of **100 input / 10 output**, then **250 input / 25 output**, hosting reports **350 input / 35 output — 385 total**.

The framework's `AgentResponse.from_updates` correctly reports **250 input / 25 output — 275 total** for the same updates.

This affects reported usage. The reproduction does not establish increased model consumption or billing.

## Expected Behavior

Honor usage merge semantics consistently with framework aggregation:

- `replace`: replace the previous usage snapshot.
- `append`: add incremental usage.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the following offline code with the package versions listed below. No credentials, model calls, tools, or Azure resources are needed.

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
import asyncio
from copy import deepcopy

from agent_framework import AgentResponse, AgentResponseUpdate, Content
from agent_framework_foundry_hosting._responses import _OutputItemTracker
from azure.ai.agentserver.responses.aio.streaming import ResponseEventStream


async def main():
    contents = [
        Content.from_usage(
            {"input_token_count": n, "output_token_count": n // 10},
            merge_mode="replace",
        )
        for n in (100, 250)
    ]

    stream = ResponseEventStream(response_id="offline-repro")
    stream.emit_created()
    stream.emit_in_progress()
    tracker = _OutputItemTracker(stream)

    for content in contents:
        async for _ in tracker.handle(content):
            pass

    framework = AgentResponse.from_updates([
        AgentResponseUpdate(message_id="turn-1", contents=[deepcopy(c)])
        for c in contents
    ])

    print("Hosting:", tracker.usage)
    print("Framework:", framework.usage_details)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Relevant values from the output:

```text
Hosting:   input_tokens=350, output_tokens=35, total_tokens=385
Framework: input_token_count=250, output_token_count=25
```

## Error Messages and Stack Traces

No exception; the reported token counts are silently inflated.

## Package Versions

```text
agent-framework-core==1.25.0
agent-framework-foundry-hosting==1.0.0b261106
azure-ai-agentserver-core==2.3.0
azure-ai-agentserver-responses==2.4.0
```

Core and hosting versions matched the latest PyPI releases when checked on November 9, 2026.

## Python Version

Python 3.14.10.

## Operating System

macOS.

## Regression

Unknown. Also reproduced with hosting `1.0.0b261030`.

## Additional Context

The [hosting usage branch](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/924a6e50ec0336f3c965ee8b1151c54085888b6e/python/packages/foundry_hosting/agent_framework_foundry_hosting/_responses.py#L3054-L3055) unconditionally calls `add_usage_details`.

Related reports:

- **microsoft/agent-framework#7143**, fixed by **microsoft/agent-framework#7162**: analogous cumulative-usage bug in the Anthropic client, not this hosting branch. Anthropic is not involved in this reproduction.
- **microsoft/agent-framework#9980**: replacement updates corrupt function-call arguments in the same hosting adapter. The usage defect reproduces without function calls.

A search of open and closed issues, PRs, and relevant comments did not identify an exact duplicate.

**Possible direction**

My understanding is that the hosting tracker may need to respect `merge_mode` when processing usage updates. One possible approach would be to replace the accumulated usage for replacement snapshots while continuing to add incremental updates, similar to framework aggregation.

I may be missing hosting-specific considerations, so I'd appreciate maintainer guidance on whether this interpretation and approach are appropriate. Tests covering replacement snapshots, incremental updates, and mixed updates could help validate the intended behavior.

**AI assistance:** GitHub Copilot assisted with analysis, duplicate research, the reproduction, and this report. The reproduction was executed locally against the versions above.

issue.title: `DELETE /api/sources/{id}` returns 200 although the source was not deleted (SurrealDB transaction conflict while the worker writes embeddings)

labels.name: repo-bbd6f5d6
labels.description: Approved and ready to be worked on

issue.body:
## Environment

Open Notebook `lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest` (1.15), SurrealDB 2.7.0 (RocksDB), `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_WORKER_MAX_TASKS=1`,
Voyage AI embeddings (`OPEN_NOTEBOOK_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE=96`), ~58k chunks in `source_embedding`.

## What happens

When a source is deleted while the worker is writing embeddings for another source, SurrealDB can reject the
delete transaction with a retryable conflict. The API logs the failure but still answers **200 OK**, and the
source (with all its chunks) is still there:

```
22:55:55.141 INFO     open_notebook.domain.notebook:delete:658 - Deleted file for source source:vv0lnvtj4jbev6lyu473: /app/data/uploads/Informationandadvicedj2004.pdf
22:55:58.175 WARNING  open_notebook.domain.notebook:delete:682 - Failed to delete embeddings/insights for source source:vv0lnvtj4jbev6lyu473: The query was not executed due to a failed transaction. Failed to commit transaction due to a read or write conflict. This transaction can be retried
22:55:58.175 DEBUG    open_notebook.domain.base:delete:215 - Deleting record with id source:vv0lnvtj4jbev6lyu473
INFO:     "DELETE /api/sources/source%3Avv0lnvtj4jbev6lyu473 HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     "GET /api/sources/source%3Avv0lnvtj4jbev6lyu473 HTTP/1.1" 200 OK        ← still exists, 59 chunks left
```

In a batch of 10 deletions issued while embeddings for 10 new sources were being written, **3 of 10** returned 200
without deleting anything: each logged the warning above, yet the source record and all its `source_embedding`
rows were still present afterwards (102, 166 and 59 chunks). The uploaded file *was* removed, so the remaining
source points to a missing asset. (Log timestamps are UTC.)
Re-issuing the same `DELETE` once the worker was idle deleted them (0 chunks left).

The create path behaves better: `POST /api/sources/json` returns **500** with the same retryable conflict
(`repo_create: … read or write conflict. This transaction can be retried`), so the client knows to retry.

## Reproduction

1. Upload a large document so that `embed_source` runs for a minute or more (e.g. a 200-page PDF, ~1,900 chunks).
2. While that `embed_source` command is `running`, delete several other existing sources, one after another:
   `DELETE /api/sources/{id}` for each.
3. For each, call `GET /api/sources/{id}` and count its chunks:
   `SELECT count() FROM source_embedding WHERE source = <id> GROUP ALL;`
4. Some deletions answer 200 but the source and its chunks remain (3/10 in our run).

## Expected

- Retry the delete on SurrealDB's retryable conflict (the error says *"This transaction can be retried"*), and/or
- return an error status (409 or 500) when the source record or its embeddings were not deleted,
- and delete the uploaded file only after the database records are gone.

## Workaround we use

Every deletion is verified by re-reading (`GET` must return 404 and the chunk count must be 0) and retried with
backoff; bulk deletions are only issued once no `embed_source` command is running.

## Related observation

`POST /api/sources/json` with text content containing a NUL byte (`\x00`, e.g. from some PDF text extractions)
fails with 500 *"Failed to queue processing"* (`Serialization error: to be serialized string contained a null
byte`), after the source record has been validated. Stripping control characters before queuing the command, or
returning a 422 that names the problem, would make this easier to diagnose.

Worse, the failed request still leaves a `command` row (`process_source`, status `new`) whose `args` contain the
NUL byte, while no `source` record exists for it. From then on the worker's poll query
(`SELECT * FROM command WHERE status = 'new' ORDER BY created ASC`) fails with the same serialization error on
every iteration, the worker exits, and supervisord gives up (`worker entered FATAL state`). Container restarts do
not help: a single rejected upload turns into a permanent outage of all background processing until someone deletes
the orphan row by hand. (Observed on v1-latest, 2026-10-16: six retries of one upload left six such rows.) Writing the
`command` row only after the content has been validated, or at least cleaning up the row when the request fails,
would prevent this.

Its file-ordering check is already covered by #1559's tests.

issue.title: fix(core): send status text body for HTTP exception responses
issue.body:
#### Short description of what this changes or resolves:

Fixes #11952. `ErrorHandler::buildResponse()` returned `HttpExceptionInterface` responses with no body, so AJAX and API callers got a status code and nothing else.

#### Changes proposed in this pull request:

- The body of an `HttpExceptionInterface` response now holds the status reason phrase, for example `Not Found`. Unknown status codes get `An error has occurred.`.
- The exception message is added only when error display is on, matching the 500 path.
- The exception message is not sent by default. AGENTS.md forbids exposing `getMessage()` to users, and messages such as `Controller not found: <class>` leak internal names. This differs from the issue's suggested fix, which sends the message for 4xx.
- `OpenEMR\Common\Http\Psr17Factory::createResponse()` no longer forwards an empty reason phrase to Nyholm. Nyholm only fills in the standard phrase when the argument is omitted, so the production factory returned an empty phrase for every code.
- `buildResponse()` is now public so the isolated tests can call it without exiting the process.
- `Psr17FactoryIsolatedTest` covers empty, custom, and unknown-code phrases. `ErrorHandlerTest` uses the production factories from `ServiceContainer`.
- Five isolated tests in `ErrorHandlerTest` cover reason-phrase bodies, header retention, unknown status codes, the display-errors detail, and the generic 500.

Verification:
- `ErrorHandlerTest`: 9 tests, 19 assertions, pass.
- Full isolated suite: 8945 tests pass. Seven warnings come from `ViewRendererListenerTest`, which this change does not touch.
- PHPStan, full codebase, level max: no errors.
- phpcs and rector dry-run on the changed files: clean.

#### Was an AI assistant used? Yes / No

Yes. The commit has an `Assisted-by: Claude Code` trailer.

comment.body: @coderabbitai Confirmed and fixed in 495ae47. I checked it with PHP's built-in server: after `header('Content-Type: text/html')`, a second `header('Content-Type: text/plain', false)` sent both headers. `handleException()` now takes its header lines from a new `headerLines()`. The first value of each header replaces one the page already set. `Set-Cookie` always adds, so earlier cookies such as the session are kept. The same server check now sends one Content-Type and keeps the earlier cookie. Three new tests cover replace, multi-value and Set-Cookie. issue.title: fix(utilities): keep primitives unchanged at max_depth in to_serializable
issue.body:
Fixes #9107

The depth check ran before the primitive check, so numbers, strings, booleans and `None` at the depth limit became `repr()` strings (`['query']` was recorded as `["'query'"]`). Primitives are now returned before the depth limit applies. 2 new tests fail on `main` and pass now; `test_serialization.py` is 28 passed, ruff clean. The 10 telemetry and events test failures on my machine are identical on `main`.

Second commit, from [this comment on #9107](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/issues/9107#issuecomment-6672657800): `LLMCallStartedEvent` serialized `tools` with the default `max_depth=5`. Each property schema sits at depth 5 (`tools -> tool -> function -> parameters -> properties`), so dicts there became repr strings such as `"{'title': 'Productname', 'type': 'string'}"`. `_emit_call_started_event` now serializes `tools` with no depth limit; cycle detection still applies. The new test in `tests/events/test_llm_finish_reason_response_id.py` fails on `main` with that repr and passes now.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Serialization and event-payload shaping only; no changes to LLM calls, auth, or business logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`to_serializable`** now resolves primitives (`str`, numbers, booleans, `None`, UUIDs, datetimes) before the recursion depth cutoff, so values at the default depth limit stay typed JSON values instead of being turned into `repr()` strings (e.g. `required` name lists no longer become quoted strings).
> 
> **LLM call telemetry** serializes `tools` on `LLMCallStartedEvent` with `max_depth=0` so deeply nested function parameter schemas are emitted intact rather than truncated at depth 5.
> 
> New tests cover depth behavior, tool schema round-tripping in `_emit_call_started_event`, and that containers still truncate when the limit is hit.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b6ed49f7ce5850f91c665da46715008d51d11d6b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

On the recursion limit: crewAI already serializes with `max_depth=0` in `flow/expressions.py` and `flow/runtime/_outputs.py`, so I kept the same approach here. Each nested object adds two levels, so a tool schema would need about 500 nested objects to hit it. issue.title: [BUG] to_serializable turns primitives at max_depth into repr strings
issue.body:
### Description

`to_serializable` turns primitive leaves into their `repr()` string once `max_depth` is reached. Numbers become `'1'`, strings gain quotes, `True` becomes `'True'`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
from crewai.utilities.serialization import to_serializable
to_serializable({"a": {"b": {"c": {"d": {"n": 1, "s": "x", "ok": True, "z": None}}}}})
```

### Expected behavior

Leaves are returned unchanged: `{'n': 1, 's': 'x', 'ok': True, 'z': None}`.

### Screenshots/Code snippets

Actual: `{'n': '1', 's': "'x'", 'ok': 'True', 'z': 'None'}`. A tool schema's `"required": ["query"]` inside `LLMCallStartedEvent` is recorded as `["'query'"]`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.13

### crewAI Version

1.15.35 (main)

### crewAI Tools Version

main (same monorepo checkout)

### Virtual Environment

Venv (uv)

### Evidence

The depth check runs before the primitive check, so primitives at the limit take the repr fallback. Tests in the linked branch fail on `main` with `assert ["'query'"] == ['query']`.

### Possible Solution

Check for primitives before the depth limit. Branch: https://github.com/Mahdi-Hasan/crewAI/tree/fix/to-serializable-depth-limit-primitives

### Additional context

I searched issues and PRs for `to_serializable`; related ones are #7652 (Enum values, closed) and open PRs about Enum and CEL state, which touch different branches of the function.

## Summary
Files that start with a UTF-8 byte order mark are not parsed. The config and preferences files become "unreadable", and a command's frontmatter is treated as part of the prompt body.

1. Write `agents.config.json` with a leading BOM (`\uFEFF`), for example with Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`. Set `nanocoder.retries.maxEmptyTurns` to 7.

BOM files load like the same file without a BOM (value 7; description and aliases read from the frontmatter).

```
nanocoder.retries.maxEmptyTurns
  value    2            <- default; 7 expected
  layer    default

config diff:  global ...\agents.config.json   unreadable: Unexpected token '﻿', "﻿{"nanocod"... is not valid JSON
```
The BOM command parses with no metadata, and its content is `---\ndescription: BOM command\naliases:\n  - bc\n---\nDo the thing`. A spec calling `splitFrontmatter('\uFEFF---\ndescription: Hello\n---\nBody')` fails:

issue.title: [BUG] Plan-and-Execute replans again after every parallel batch because earlier failures are counted again
issue.body:
### Description
`AgentExecutor._should_replan` asks for a replan when two or more todos have status `failed`, or have a result that starts with `Error:`.
A replan keeps failed todos as history (`TodoList.replace_pending_todos`), so those same todos are counted again on every later check.

After the first replan, the next `_should_replan` call returns `True` again, even when every step of the new plan succeeded.
Each of these replans calls the planner, increments `replan_count` and replaces the pending steps of the plan that was working.
This repeats until `replan_count` reaches `max_replans` (3 by default).
The docstring says "Multiple consecutive todo failures"; the code counts every failure in the history.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run an agent with `planning=True` and a plan whose steps run in parallel (several steps ready at once).
2. Let two steps fail, so `after_parallel_execution` asks for a replan.
3. Let the replanned steps all succeed.
4. `after_parallel_execution` returns `needs_replan` again.

```python
print(t.AgentExecutor.after_parallel_execution(executor))
```

Two new failures still trigger a replan.

issue.title: [BUG] Replanning restarts step numbers at 1, so new plan steps alias the preserved completed steps
issue.body:
### Description
`TodoList.replace_pending_todos` keeps the completed, failed and running steps and appends the replanned ones.
The planner schema asks for 1-based `step_number`, so a replan usually restarts at 1.
The list then holds duplicate step numbers, for example `[1, 2, 1, 2, 3]`.

Every lookup uses `get_by_step_number`, which returns the first match.
New steps therefore alias the preserved ones:

- `get_ready_todos` sees a new step's dependency as the old, finished step. New steps that depend on each other are all "ready" at once.
- `mark_running` and `mark_completed` change the old step. The new step stays pending and is picked again. The old result is overwritten.
- `state.observations` and `execution_log` are keyed by step number and mix old and new steps.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run an agent with `planning=True` (Plan-and-Execute path in `AgentExecutor`).
2. Let step 1 complete and step 2 fail, so the observer asks for a replan.
3. The planner returns the revised plan with steps numbered 1, 2, 3 (step 2 depends on 1, step 3 on 2).
4. The executor calls `replace_pending_todos` with these steps.

The same state can be built without an LLM:

```python
from crewai.utilities.planning_types import TodoItem, TodoList

todos = TodoList(items=[
    TodoItem(step_number=1, description="old 1", status="completed", result="A"),
    TodoItem(step_number=2, description="old 2", status="failed", result="Error"),
    TodoItem(step_number=3, description="old 3"),
])
todos.replace_pending_todos([
    TodoItem(step_number=1, description="new 1"),
    TodoItem(step_number=2, description="new 2", depends_on=[1]),
    TodoItem(step_number=3, description="new 3", depends_on=[2]),
])
print([t.step_number for t in todos.items])
print([t.description for t in todos.get_ready_todos()])
todos.mark_running(1)
print([(t.description, t.status) for t in todos.items])
```

### Expected behavior
- Step numbers stay unique after a replan.
- Only `new 1` is ready. `new 2` waits for `new 1`.
- `mark_running(<new step>)` changes the new step and leaves `old 1` completed.

### Screenshots/Code snippets
Output on main:

```
[1, 2, 1, 2, 3]
['new 1', 'new 2', 'new 3']
[('old 1', 'running'), ('old 2', 'failed'), ('new 1', 'pending'), ('new 2', 'pending'), ('new 3', 'pending')]
```

Through the executor (`_trigger_replan` with a mocked `AgentReasoning` that returns steps 1, 2, 3), `get_ready_todos_method` returns `multiple_todos_ready` instead of `single_todo_ready`.
`execute_todos_parallel` then runs all three new steps at once. It marks and completes the old items, so the new items stay pending.

### Operating System
Windows 11

### Python Version
3.13 (the form lists 3.10 to 3.12, nothing in the code depends on it)

### crewAI Version
1.15.35 (main at 6bd60b223).

### crewAI Tools Version
1.15.35

### Virtual Environment
Venv (uv)

### Evidence
Tests on main (new tests from the fix branch run against unfixed code):

```
FAILED test_planning_types.py::TestReplacePendingTodos::test_restarted_numbering_does_not_collide_with_preserved_steps
FAILED test_planning_types.py::TestReplacePendingTodos::test_only_first_new_step_is_ready_after_restarted_numbering
FAILED test_planning_types.py::TestReplacePendingTodos::test_marking_a_new_step_running_leaves_preserved_steps_alone
FAILED test_planning_types.py::TestReplacePendingTodos::test_completing_a_new_step_does_not_touch_preserved_results
FAILED test_planning_types.py::TestReplacePendingTodos::test_running_step_keeps_its_number_when_plan_is_replaced
FAILED test_agent_executor.py::TestReplanKeepsStepNumbersUnique (3 tests)
AssertionError: assert 'multiple_todos_ready' == 'single_todo_ready'
assert 5 == 3  where 5 = len([1, 2, 1, 2, 3])
```

### Possible Solution
In `replace_pending_todos`, when a new step number collides with a preserved one, renumber the new steps after the highest preserved number.
Remap `depends_on` entries that point at other new steps.
Leave a replan alone when it already continues the numbering (3, 4, 5 after steps 1 and 2).

### Additional context
No existing replan test covers `replace_pending_todos` or `_trigger_replan`.
Searches run (all without a match for this bug):
- `gh issue list --state all --search "replan step_number"`: only #8088 (unrelated, parallel planning and tool_failure_policy).
- `gh pr list --state all --search "replace_pending_todos"`: only #4817 and #4450 (the original feature PRs).
- `gh issue list --state all --search "completed step replan duplicate"`: nothing relevant.
- Local grep of all 2821 issue and 4000 PR titles for `replan`, `todo`, `step_number`, `depends_on`, `renumber`: no match.
- `git log --since=45.days -- lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/planning_types.py`: no commits.

issue.title: [BUG] After upgrading from a yanked release, every run reports the new version as yanked for 24 hours
issue.body:
### Description
The PyPI check keeps one cache file (`version_cache.json`) with the latest version and whether the installed version is yanked.
`get_latest_version_from_pypi` trusts any cache younger than 24 hours that has a `current_version` key, whichever version wrote it.

`is_current_version_yanked` notices the cache was written for another version and calls `get_latest_version_from_pypi` to refresh it.
That call returns straight from the same cache, so nothing is fetched, and the old yanked flag is read back.

After upgrading from a yanked release, the console prints the red "Yanked Version" panel on every run for up to 24 hours.
It names the new version and shows the old release's reason.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a yanked crewAI release once, so the cache holds `current_version_yanked: true`.
2. Upgrade to a good release (`uv sync --upgrade-package crewai`).
3. Run any crew or flow with the console output on.

Without installing anything, the same state:

```python
import json, tempfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
import crewai_core.version as v

cache = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "version_cache.json"
cache.write_text(json.dumps({
    "version": "2.0.0", "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    "current_version": "1.0.0", "current_version_yanked": True,
    "current_version_yanked_reason": "bad release"}))
releases = {"releases": {"1.0.0": [{"yanked": True, "yanked_reason": "bad release"}],
                         "2.0.0": [{"yanked": False}]}}
resp = MagicMock()
resp.__enter__.return_value.read.return_value = json.dumps(releases).encode()
with patch.object(v, "_get_cache_file", return_value=cache), \
     patch.object(v, "get_crewai_version", return_value="2.0.0"), \
     patch.object(v.request, "urlopen", return_value=resp) as urlopen:
    print(v.is_current_version_yanked(), "urlopen calls:", urlopen.call_count)
```

### Expected behavior
`2.0.0` is not yanked, so the result is `(False, "")`.
The cache from `1.0.0` is not used, and PyPI is queried once to rewrite it.

### Screenshots/Code snippets
Output on main:

```
(True, 'bad release') urlopen calls: 0
```

The panel comes from `ConsoleFormatter` (`crewai/events/utils/console_formatter.py`):

```
Version 2.0.0 has been yanked from PyPI.
Reason: bad release

To update, run: uv sync --upgrade-package crewai
```

### Operating System
Windows 11

### Python Version
3.13 (the form lists 3.10 to 3.12, nothing in the code depends on it)

### crewAI Version
1.15.35 (main at 6bd60b223).

### crewAI Tools Version
1.15.35

### Virtual Environment
Venv (uv)

### Evidence
Tests added on the fix branch, run against unfixed code:

```
FAILED test_version.py::TestVersionCacheAfterUpgrade::test_upgrading_from_a_yanked_version_clears_the_yanked_flag   assert True is False
FAILED test_version.py::TestVersionCacheAfterUpgrade::test_cache_written_for_another_version_is_not_used_offline    assert True is False
FAILED test_version.py::TestVersionCacheAfterUpgrade::test_latest_version_is_refetched_for_a_new_installed_version  assert '2.0.0' == '3.0.0'
```

The existing `test_triggers_fetch_on_stale_cache` hides this: it mocks `get_latest_version_from_pypi`, so the cache short-circuit never runs.

### Possible Solution
In `get_latest_version_from_pypi`, use the cache only when `cache_data["current_version"] == get_crewai_version()`.
An upgrade then fetches once and rewrites the file.
In `is_current_version_yanked`, return `(False, "")` when the fetch failed and the cache still belongs to another version.

### Additional context
The cache also drives the "update available" check, so it is read the same way there. The yanked panel is the visible symptom.
Searches run (no match for this bug):
- `gh issue list --state all --search "yanked version after upgrade"`, `"version_cache.json"`, `"is_current_version_yanked"`, `"yanked panel stale cache"`: no issues.
- `gh pr list` with the same terms: only #4464 (the original yank detection) and #4884 (CLI extraction).
- Local grep of all issue and PR titles for `yank`, `version cache`, `pypi`: no match.
- `git log --since=60.days` on `crewai_core/version.py`: only #9029, unrelated.

issue.title: OpenAIChatCompletionsModel sends tool_choice without tools, which the API rejects, on turns with no tools
issue.body:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #4326 (fixed by #4359 and #4330) covered the same API rule for `parallel_tool_calls`. `tool_choice` was left out.

### Describe the bug

`OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` always sends `ModelSettings.tool_choice`, even when the converted tool list is empty and `tools` is left out of the request. The Chat Completions API rejects that combination:

```text
Invalid value for 'tool_choice': 'tool_choice' is only allowed when 'tools' are specified.
```

So an app-wide `RunConfig(model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="auto"))` breaks every turn of an agent that has no function tools and no handoffs in that turn. Examples are a final summarizer agent after a handoff, or an agent whose tools are all switched off with `is_enabled`. `parallel_tool_calls` is already omitted in this case. `LitellmModel` sends the same request; I checked the body LiteLLM actually posts. `AnyLLMModel`'s chat path has the same line, but I didn't run it.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` (e355d69), also 0.24.0
- Related library versions: openai 3.29.0, litellm 1.83.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating system: macOS
- Model and model provider: any Chat Completions model (`OpenAIChatCompletionsModel`, `LitellmModel`)
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

### Repro steps

A real `AsyncOpenAI` client on an `httpx2.MockTransport`, printing what's sent:

```python
import asyncio, json
import httpx2
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, ModelSettings, OpenAIChatCompletionsModel, RunConfig, Runner

def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
    body = json.loads(request.content)
    print("tools in request:", "tools" in body, "| tool_choice:", body.get("tool_choice"),
          "| parallel_tool_calls in request:", "parallel_tool_calls" in body)
    return httpx2.Response(200, json={
        "id": "chatcmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
        "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                     "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "OK"}}],
    })

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler)))
    agent = Agent(name="Summarizer", instructions="Reply OK",
                  model=OpenAIChatCompletionsModel("gpt-4o-mini", client))
    cfg = RunConfig(tracing_disabled=True,
                    model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="auto", parallel_tool_calls=False))
    await Runner.run(agent, "Say OK.", run_config=cfg)

asyncio.run(main())
```

```text
tools in request: False | tool_choice: auto | parallel_tool_calls in request: False
```

### Expected behavior

`tool_choice` is left out when the request has no tools, the same way `parallel_tool_calls` already is.

### Root cause and a possible fix

`tool_choice` is converted at [openai_chatcompletions.py#L642](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L642) and sent at [#L709](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L709), while only `parallel_tool_calls` is gated on `converted_tools` ([#L652-L656](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L652-L656)). LiteLLM: [litellm_model.py#L646](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py#L646). AnyLLM: [any_llm_model.py#L951](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/extensions/models/any_llm_model.py#L951).

```diff
--- a/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py
+++ b/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py
@@ -654,6 +654,9 @@ class OpenAIChatCompletionsModel(Model):
         parallel_tool_calls: bool | Omit = (
             self._non_null_or_omit(model_settings.parallel_tool_calls) if converted_tools else omit
         )
+        # The API rejects tool_choice without tools, the same as parallel_tool_calls.
+        if not converted_tools:
+            tool_choice = omit
--- a/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py
+++ b/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py
@@ -643,7 +643,7 @@ class LitellmModel(Model):
-            tool_choice=self._remove_not_given(tool_choice),
+            tool_choice=self._remove_not_given(tool_choice) if converted_tools else None,
```

With that change, both repros send no `tool_choice`, and `tests/models` passes (1023 passed, 1 skipped). The placeholder `Response.tool_choice` built for streaming is separate and unchanged.

issue.title: [BUG] cleanup_expired_files(delete_from_provider=True) never deletes from the provider
issue.body:
### Description

`cleanup_expired_files(cache, delete_from_provider=True)` never calls the provider's `delete` for expired entries. It clears the cache entry, so the uploaded file is orphaned at the provider.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an `UploadCache` and `cache.set(...)` an entry whose `expires_at` is a moment ahead.
2. Wait until it has expired.
3. Call `cleanup_expired_files(cache, delete_from_provider=True)` with an uploader for that provider.

### Expected behavior

`uploader.delete(file_id)` is called for each expired entry, then the entry is removed.

### Screenshots/Code snippets

Regression test in the linked branch fails on `main` with `assert [] == ['expired-file']`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.13

### crewAI Version

1.15.35 (main)

### crewAI Tools Version

main (same monorepo checkout)

### Virtual Environment

Venv (uv)

### Evidence

The expired list comes from `get_all_for_provider()`, which already drops expired entries. The sync wrapper's event loop also closes before the TTL timer fires, so the backend still holds the entry when cleanup runs.

### Possible Solution

Collect expired entries without the expiry filter before deleting. Branch: https://github.com/Mahdi-Hasan/crewAI/tree/fix/cleanup-expired-files-provider-delete . Note #8715 edits the same two files for a different problem (provider scoping), so the second PR to land may need a small rebase.

### Additional context

Found by reading `crewai_files/cache`. I searched issues and PRs for `cleanup_expired_files`, `delete_from_provider` and `UploadCache`; the only related one is the closed #6742 about sync wrapper deadlocks.

issue.title: BatchModelRequests status-check throttle skips checks on Windows for sub-15ms poll intervals

labels.name: repo-e17188c0
labels.description: Pydanty could not complete issue triage

issue.body:
`tests/models/test_batch.py::test_a_streamed_run_can_end_pending_and_be_collected_later` fails every time on Windows (3 of 3 runs on current `main`). The run ends pending on every resume and `status_checks` stays at 1.

**Cause.** `_batch_model.py` throttles status checks with `time.monotonic() - checked_at < poll_interval`. On Windows `time.get_clock_info('monotonic')` reports a resolution of 0.015625s, so two readings in the same tick differ by 0. With the 1ms `FAST_POLLING` settings the throttle then treats every check as too recent and returns the cached status.

**Impact.** Test-only in practice, since real poll intervals are seconds or minutes. It stops Windows contributors from getting a green `tests/models/test_batch.py`.

**Proposed fix.** Use `time.perf_counter()` in the two places (same monotonic guarantee, finer tick). With it, `tests/models/test_batch.py` and `tests/models/test_openai_batch.py` pass (151). Branch: https://github.com/Mahdi-Hasan/pydantic-ai/tree/fix/batch-poll-throttle-windows-clock

issue.title: OpenAIConversationsSession and OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession ignore set_default_openai_key()
issue.body:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. Nothing covers it. #2164 is a feature request for several keys per run.

### Describe the bug

`set_default_openai_key()` is documented as the key that "will be used instead of the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable". `OpenAIProvider` honors it, and so do the voice provider and the Codex tool. `OpenAIConversationsSession` and `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` don't. When no default *client* is set, they build a bare `AsyncOpenAI()`, which reads only `OPENAI_API_KEY`. That causes two problems:

- When the key is set only through the SDK, `OpenAIConversationsSession()` raises `OpenAIError: Missing credentials` when it's constructed, and the compaction session raises on its first `responses.compact` call.
- When `OPENAI_API_KEY` is also set, the sessions quietly use the environment key while model calls use the SDK key. Conversation items and the billed `responses.compact` calls land in a different project or org than the run's responses.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` (e355d69), also 0.24.0
- Related library versions: openai 3.29.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating system: macOS
- Model and model provider: OpenAI
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

### Repro steps

```python
import os
os.environ.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)  # key is configured only through the SDK

from agents import SQLiteSession, set_default_openai_key
from agents.memory import OpenAIConversationsSession, OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession
from agents.models.multi_provider import MultiProvider

set_default_openai_key("sk-from-set-default-openai-key")

def show(label, make):
    try:
        print(f"{label}:", make().api_key)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{label}:", type(e).__name__, "-", str(e)[:40])

for phase in ("SDK key only", "OPENAI_API_KEY also set"):
    if phase == "OPENAI_API_KEY also set":
        os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "sk-other-project-from-env"
    print("--", phase)
    print("model client        :", MultiProvider().get_model("gpt-4.1")._client.api_key)
    show("ConversationsSession", lambda: OpenAIConversationsSession()._openai_client)
    show("CompactionSession   ", lambda: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession("s", SQLiteSession("s")).client)
```

```text
-- SDK key only
model client        : sk-from-set-default-openai-key
ConversationsSession: OpenAIError - Missing credentials. Please pass a
CompactionSession   : OpenAIError - Missing credentials. Please pass a
-- OPENAI_API_KEY also set
model client        : sk-from-set-default-openai-key
ConversationsSession: sk-other-project-from-env
CompactionSession   : sk-other-project-from-env
```

### Expected behavior

With no client passed and no default client set, both sessions use the key from `set_default_openai_key()`, as model calls do.

### Root cause and a possible fix

The sessions fall back to `AsyncOpenAI()`: [openai_conversations_session.py#L21](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py#L21), [#L50](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py#L50) and [openai_responses_compaction_session.py#L196](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py#L196). The provider passes `get_default_openai_key()` instead ([openai_provider.py#L156-L161](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_provider.py#L156-L161)).

```diff
--- a/src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py
+++ b/src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py
-from agents.models._openai_shared import get_default_openai_client
+from agents.models._openai_shared import get_default_openai_client, get_default_openai_key
@@ async def start_openai_conversations_session(
-        _maybe_openai_client = default_client if default_client is not None else AsyncOpenAI()
+        _maybe_openai_client = (
+            default_client
+            if default_client is not None
+            else AsyncOpenAI(api_key=get_default_openai_key())
+        )
@@ class OpenAIConversationsSession(SessionABC):
-            _openai_client = default_client if default_client is not None else AsyncOpenAI()
+            _openai_client = (
+                default_client
+                if default_client is not None
+                else AsyncOpenAI(api_key=get_default_openai_key())
+            )
--- a/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py
+++ b/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py
-from ..models._openai_shared import get_default_openai_client
+from ..models._openai_shared import get_default_openai_client, get_default_openai_key
@@ def client(self) -> AsyncOpenAI:
-            self._client = default_client if default_client is not None else AsyncOpenAI()
+            self._client = (
+                default_client
+                if default_client is not None
+                else AsyncOpenAI(api_key=get_default_openai_key())
+            )
```

`AsyncOpenAI(api_key=None)` still falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so nothing changes for callers who haven't set a default key. With the patch, both sessions report the SDK key in both phases, and `tests/memory` passes (444 passed).

comment.body: Root-cause analysis and a proposed patch, since the contributing guide limits PRs to maintainers. `OpenAIConversationsSession` and `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` build a bare `AsyncOpenAI()` in three places, so they never see the key from `set_default_openai_key()`. The patch passes `api_key=get_default_openai_key()`; when no SDK key is set that is `None`, so the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback still works. 5 tests included (4 fail on `main`). Branch: https://github.com/Mahdi-Hasan/openai-agents-python/tree/fix/sessions-default-openai-key

issue.title: OpenAIChatCompletionsModel sends tool_choice without tools, which the API rejects, on turns with no tools
issue.body:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #4326 (fixed by #4359 and #4330) covered the same API rule for `parallel_tool_calls`. `tool_choice` was left out.

### Describe the bug

`OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` always sends `ModelSettings.tool_choice`, even when the converted tool list is empty and `tools` is left out of the request. The Chat Completions API rejects that combination:

```text
Invalid value for 'tool_choice': 'tool_choice' is only allowed when 'tools' are specified.
```

So an app-wide `RunConfig(model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="auto"))` breaks every turn of an agent that has no function tools and no handoffs in that turn. Examples are a final summarizer agent after a handoff, or an agent whose tools are all switched off with `is_enabled`. `parallel_tool_calls` is already omitted in this case. `LitellmModel` sends the same request; I checked the body LiteLLM actually posts. `AnyLLMModel`'s chat path has the same line, but I didn't run it.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` (e355d69), also 0.24.0
- Related library versions: openai 3.29.0, litellm 1.83.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating system: macOS
- Model and model provider: any Chat Completions model (`OpenAIChatCompletionsModel`, `LitellmModel`)
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

### Repro steps

A real `AsyncOpenAI` client on an `httpx2.MockTransport`, printing what's sent:

```python
import asyncio, json
import httpx2
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, ModelSettings, OpenAIChatCompletionsModel, RunConfig, Runner

def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
    body = json.loads(request.content)
    print("tools in request:", "tools" in body, "| tool_choice:", body.get("tool_choice"),
          "| parallel_tool_calls in request:", "parallel_tool_calls" in body)
    return httpx2.Response(200, json={
        "id": "chatcmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
        "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                     "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "OK"}}],
    })

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler)))
    agent = Agent(name="Summarizer", instructions="Reply OK",
                  model=OpenAIChatCompletionsModel("gpt-4o-mini", client))
    cfg = RunConfig(tracing_disabled=True,
                    model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="auto", parallel_tool_calls=False))
    await Runner.run(agent, "Say OK.", run_config=cfg)

asyncio.run(main())
```

```text
tools in request: False | tool_choice: auto | parallel_tool_calls in request: False
```

### Expected behavior

`tool_choice` is left out when the request has no tools, the same way `parallel_tool_calls` already is.

### Root cause and a possible fix

`tool_choice` is converted at [openai_chatcompletions.py#L642](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L642) and sent at [#L709](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L709), while only `parallel_tool_calls` is gated on `converted_tools` ([#L652-L656](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py#L652-L656)). LiteLLM: [litellm_model.py#L646](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py#L646). AnyLLM: [any_llm_model.py#L951](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/extensions/models/any_llm_model.py#L951).

```diff
--- a/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py
+++ b/src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py
@@ -654,6 +654,9 @@ class OpenAIChatCompletionsModel(Model):
         parallel_tool_calls: bool | Omit = (
             self._non_null_or_omit(model_settings.parallel_tool_calls) if converted_tools else omit
         )
+        # The API rejects tool_choice without tools, the same as parallel_tool_calls.
+        if not converted_tools:
+            tool_choice = omit
--- a/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py
+++ b/src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py
@@ -643,7 +643,7 @@ class LitellmModel(Model):
-            tool_choice=self._remove_not_given(tool_choice),
+            tool_choice=self._remove_not_given(tool_choice) if converted_tools else None,
```

With that change, both repros send no `tool_choice`, and `tests/models` passes (1023 passed, 1 skipped). The placeholder `Response.tool_choice` built for streaming is separate and unchanged.

comment.body: Root-cause analysis and a proposed patch, since the contributing guide limits PRs to maintainers. `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` passes `tool_choice` through even when the converted tool list is empty, which the API rejects. The patch omits it in that case, the same guard `parallel_tool_calls` already has. `LitellmModel` and `AnyLLMModel` look affected too; I left them out since the title names the OpenAI model. Regression tests for the no-tools cases are included. Branch: https://github.com/Mahdi-Hasan/openai-agents-python/tree/fix/tool-choice-without-tools

issue.title: tool_choice naming a function tool called web_search, file_search, mcp, etc. selects the built-in tool instead
issue.body:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #4952 fixed this for `shell` and `apply_patch`, and `computer` and `tool_search` are already gated with tests. The other built-in names were left out.

### Describe the bug

An agent on the Responses API has a function tool whose name matches a built-in tool type, for example its own `web_search` backed by another search API. Setting `ModelSettings(tool_choice="web_search")` to force that tool sends `tool_choice={"type": "web_search"}`, which selects the hosted web search tool, instead of `{"type": "function", "name": "web_search"}`. The request's `tools` list contains only the function, so the caller's tool can't be forced. The same happens for `file_search`, `web_search_preview`, `computer_use_preview` (with no `ComputerTool`), `image_generation`, `code_interpreter`, `mcp` and `programmatic_tool_calling`.

#4952 described exactly this for `shell` and `apply_patch`: without a gate, "a function tool named `shell` or `apply_patch` would silently stop being targetable".

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` (e355d69), also 0.24.0
- Related library versions: openai 3.29.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating system: macOS
- Model and model provider: OpenAI Responses API
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

### Repro steps

A real `AsyncOpenAI` client on an `httpx2.MockTransport`, printing what's sent:

```python
import asyncio, json
import httpx2
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, ModelSettings, OpenAIResponsesModel, RunConfig, Runner, function_tool

def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
    body = json.loads(request.content)
    print("tools sent      :", [(t["type"], t.get("name")) for t in body["tools"]])
    print("tool_choice sent:", body["tool_choice"])
    return httpx2.Response(200, json={
        "id": "resp_1", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "model": "gpt-4.1",
        "status": "completed", "parallel_tool_calls": True, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [],
        "output": [{"type": "message", "id": "msg_1", "role": "assistant", "status": "completed",
                    "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok", "annotations": []}]}],
    })

@function_tool(name_override="web_search")
def my_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search my own index."""
    return "result"

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler)))
    agent = Agent(name="a", tools=[my_search], model=OpenAIResponsesModel("gpt-4.1", client),
                  model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="web_search"))
    await Runner.run(agent, "find docs", run_config=RunConfig(tracing_disabled=True))

asyncio.run(main())
```

```text
tools sent      : [('function', 'web_search')]
tool_choice sent: {'type': 'web_search'}
```

### Expected behavior

`tool_choice` is `{"type": "function", "name": "web_search"}` whenever a function tool (or handoff) with that name is configured, as already happens for `shell`, `apply_patch`, `computer` and `tool_search`.

### Root cause and a possible fix

`Converter.convert_tool_choice` maps these strings to built-in selectors before the named-function branch and doesn't look at the configured tools ([openai_responses.py#L1856-L1894](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_responses.py#L1856-L1894)). The `shell`/`apply_patch` branches are gated ([#L1895-L1902](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/e355d69152d4f4730dfb03b63dbce53e8d9f5d8c/src/agents/models/openai_responses.py#L1895-L1902)). The gate below checks that a local function tool with that name exists, not that the built-in is configured, so prompt-managed built-in tools (#1304) keep working:

```diff
--- a/src/agents/models/openai_responses.py
+++ b/src/agents/models/openai_responses.py
+# Strings that convert_tool_choice maps to a built-in tool selector without checking
+# whether that built-in tool is configured.
+_HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_NAMES = frozenset(
+    {
+        "programmatic_tool_calling",
+        "file_search",
+        "web_search",
+        "web_search_preview",
+        "computer_use_preview",
+        "image_generation",
+        "code_interpreter",
+        "mcp",
+    }
+)
@@ class Converter:
         elif tool_choice == "none":
             return "none"
+        elif tool_choice in _HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_NAMES and cls._has_top_level_function_named(
+            tool_choice, tools=tools, handoffs=handoffs
+        ):
+            # Like computer, shell and apply_patch, a function tool with a built-in tool's
+            # name must stay targetable.
+            return {"type": "function", "name": tool_choice}
         elif tool_choice == "programmatic_tool_calling":
@@ class Converter:
+    @classmethod
+    def _has_top_level_function_named(
+        cls,
+        name: str,
+        *,
+        tools: Sequence[Tool] | None,
+        handoffs: Sequence[Handoff[Any, Any]] | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return any(handoff.tool_name == name for handoff in handoffs or ()) or any(
+            isinstance(tool, FunctionTool)
+            and tool.name == name
+            and get_explicit_function_tool_namespace(tool) is None
+            and not tool.defer_loading
+            for tool in tools or ()
+        )
```

With the patch, the repro sends `{'type': 'function', 'name': 'web_search'}`. With no tools, or with a configured `WebSearchTool()`, `"web_search"` still maps to `{'type': 'web_search'}`. `tests/models` passes (1023 passed, 1 skipped).

comment.body: Root-cause analysis and a proposed patch, since the contributing guide limits PRs to maintainers. In the Responses converter, a `tool_choice` naming a function tool called `web_search`, `file_search`, `mcp` and similar is mapped to the hosted tool type before checking local function tools. The patch resolves it to the function tool when a function tool or handoff has that name; if the matching hosted tool is also present, the hosted tool still wins. I chose that over the `shell`/`apply_patch` rule because the stricter rule changes behaviour with an empty tool list. 9 regression tests included (they fail on `main`). issue.title: Close the `SqlitePlanStore` connection when its schema setup fails on a locked database

labels.name: repo-e17188c0
labels.description: Report that something isn't working, or PR implementing a fix

issue.body:
## Background
While fixing merge-queue flakes caused by `ResourceWarning: unclosed database`, #12147 made `SqliteStepStore._open()` and `SqliteMediaStore._open()` close their connection when switching a locked new database to WAL fails. The same check turned up the defect below in the planning store. CI never hit it.

## The problem
`SqlitePlanStore._connect()` (`pydantic_ai_harness.planning`) opens a connection and, on first use, runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ...` and `commit()`. When another connection holds the database locked, `CREATE TABLE` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` and the connection is never closed. The exception's traceback keeps it alive until the garbage collector finds it. Under `-W error::ResourceWarning` it then surfaces as `unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection ...>` (reproduced locally: a 0.01 s busy timeout and another connection holding `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`). Under pytest, that warning fails whatever test happens to be running when the collector runs.

## Why it's out of scope for the originating PR
#12147 fixes only the two stores on the path that produced the CI failures (clai2's session step store and its media store). The planning store was never implicated, and fixing it there would widen that PR past the reproduced defect.

## Where
- `src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/planning/_store.py`: `SqlitePlanStore._connect`

## Suggested direction (low-confidence)
Close the connection and re-raise when the schema setup fails, as #12147 does in `_open()`. Add a test that holds the database locked and checks that the connection the store opened is closed.

_Posted by CLAI on Douwe's behalf._

issue.title: OpenAI batch requests run `uname -p` on the event loop the first time `_batch_group` reads the client's `default_headers`

labels.name: repo-e17188c0
labels.description: Report that something isn't working, or PR implementing a fix

issue.body:
> This issue was posted by Claude Code using claude-opus-5-5 on behalf of David.

The first OpenAI batch request a process encodes runs `uname -p` as a subprocess on the event loop thread.

`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/_openai_batch.py :: _batch_group()` reads `client.default_headers` to hash the client's credential. On a client that has not sent a request yet, the SDK builds its platform headers by calling `get_platform()` there and then, and `platform.platform()` runs `uname -p` through `subprocess.check_output`. The SDK itself avoids this for requests: it calls `get_platform()` in a worker thread first, noting that it can block. `credential_hash` drops `user-agent` and `x-stainless-*` headers, so the platform headers this computes are discarded anyway.

```
OpenAIResponsesModel.batch_encode()          models/openai.py
└─ _openai_batch.batch_encode()
   └─ _openai_batch._batch_group()           client.default_headers
      └─ openai._base_client.platform_headers()
         └─ get_platform() -> platform.platform() -> subprocess.check_output(['uname', '-p'])   on MainThread
```

### How it shows up in tests

With BlockBuster on (local runs, and CI's 3.13 lane), BlockBuster raises `BlockingError: Blocking call to os.read` inside `Popen.__init__` after the child has started. `get_platform()` catches it and returns `'Unknown'`, so the child is never waited on. When the garbage collector frees that `Popen`, its `ResourceWarning` fails whichever test is running:

```
tests/models/test_batch_resume.py::test_a_stored_history_resumes_in_a_new_process_with_a_rotated_api_key
E   ResourceWarning: subprocess 386 is still running
```

On `main`, `uv run pytest tests/models/test_batch_resume.py -p no:randomly` failed 3 of 3 runs on macOS. With `BLOCKBUSTER_ENABLED=false` it passes. It only fails when no earlier test in the process has already filled `platform`'s cache, which is why CI, running the whole suite, has not hit it.

<details>
<summary>Trace of the spawn</summary>

From a scratch pytest plugin wrapping `openai._base_client.get_platform` and `subprocess.Popen.__init__`:

```
=== get_platform thread=MainThread callers=['openai.py:3399:batch_encode', '_openai_batch.py:129:batch_encode', '_openai_batch.py:340:_batch_group', '_client.py:1426:default_headers', '_base_client.py:773:default_headers', '_base_client.py:810:platform_headers', '_base_client.py:2277:platform_headers']
=== spawning ['uname', '-p'] thread=MainThread
=== Popen.__init__ raised pid=386 child_created=True: blockbuster.blockbuster.BlockingError: Blocking call to os.read
=== get_platform -> 'Unknown'
=== get_platform thread=asyncio_0 callers=[... concurrent/futures/thread.py ...]
=== spawning ['uname', '-p'] thread=asyncio_0
=== spawned pid=387
=== get_platform -> 'MacOS'
```

openai 3.31.0, Python 3.13.16.

</details>

`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/_openai_responses_websocket.py :: effective_headers()` also reads `client.default_headers`. Whether it can run before the client's first request has not been checked.

Found while fixing #12411.

issue.title: [Bug] string_replace fails multi-line edits on CRLF files and writes mixed line endings
issue.body:
## Summary
`string_replace` compares `old_str` with the raw file text. Models send LF, so a multi-line edit on a CRLF file is not found. A single-line edit that adds lines writes LF into a CRLF file.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create `a.txt` containing `one\r\ntwo\r\nthree\r\n`.
2. Call `string_replace` with `old_str: "one\ntwo"` and `new_str: "ONE\nTWO"`.
3. Create `b.txt` with the same content. Call `string_replace` with `old_str: "two"` and `new_str: "TWO\nTWO-b"`.

## Expected behaviour
1. `a.txt` becomes `ONE\r\nTWO\r\nthree\r\n`.
2. `b.txt` becomes `one\r\nTWO\r\nTWO-b\r\nthree\r\n`.

## Actual behaviour
1. The edit is refused with `Content not found in file` and `"status":"no_candidate"`, and nothing is written.
2. The file is written with mixed endings:
```
  one␍␊
- TWO␊           <- actual (LF only)
+ TWO␍␊           <- expected
  TWO-b␍␊
```
`read_file` returns the CRLF text unchanged, so the model sees `\r` it cannot easily reproduce. Any Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` has CRLF files.

## Environment
Windows 11, Node v22.22.3, Nanocoder 1.31.0 (main at 948a4e74)

## Suggested fix
- `source/tools/file-ops/string-replace.tsx:89`: detect the file's dominant line ending. Match `old_str` after converting it to that ending, instead of an exact `split(old_str)`.
- Line 106: convert `new_str` to the same ending before `replaceFirstLiteral`.
- Mention line endings in the edit-recovery evidence (`source/utils/edit-recovery.ts`).
- Add a spec with a CRLF fixture.

issue.title: fix(core): send status text body for HTTP exception responses
issue.body:
#### Short description of what this changes or resolves:

Fixes #11952. `ErrorHandler::buildResponse()` returned `HttpExceptionInterface` responses with no body, so AJAX and API callers got a status code and nothing else.

#### Changes proposed in this pull request:

- The body of an `HttpExceptionInterface` response now holds the status reason phrase, for example `Not Found`. Unknown status codes get `An error has occurred.`.
- The exception message is added only when error display is on, matching the 500 path.
- The exception message is not sent by default. AGENTS.md forbids exposing `getMessage()` to users, and messages such as `Controller not found: <class>` leak internal names. This differs from the issue's suggested fix, which sends the message for 4xx.
- `OpenEMR\Common\Http\Psr17Factory::createResponse()` no longer forwards an empty reason phrase to Nyholm. Nyholm only fills in the standard phrase when the argument is omitted, so the production factory returned an empty phrase for every code.
- `buildResponse()` is now public so the isolated tests can call it without exiting the process.
- `Psr17FactoryIsolatedTest` covers empty, custom, and unknown-code phrases. `ErrorHandlerTest` uses the production factories from `ServiceContainer`.
- Five isolated tests in `ErrorHandlerTest` cover reason-phrase bodies, header retention, unknown status codes, the display-errors detail, and the generic 500.

Verification:
- `ErrorHandlerTest`: 9 tests, 19 assertions, pass.
- Full isolated suite: 8945 tests pass. Seven warnings come from `ViewRendererListenerTest`, which this change does not touch.
- PHPStan, full codebase, level max: no errors.
- phpcs and rector dry-run on the changed files: clean.

#### Was an AI assistant used? Yes / No

Yes. The commit has an `Assisted-by: Claude Code` trailer.
